nodes.label: Initramfs Setuid Support
nodes.rationale: Set the S_ISUID bit on the initramfs inode so an execve of the file by an unprivileged user elevates the new task's euid to the file's owner (uid 0 — initramfs files are root-owned). Used for /bin/su.

nodes.label: Dynamic Direct Map Sizing
nodes.rationale: DIRECT_MAP_SIZE is runtime-sized to Multiboot2 top-of-RAM to support identity-accessible physical memory below the limit without executing extra page table work on smaller machines, while maintaining compatibility with legacy direct-map MMIO patterns below 4 GiB.

nodes.label: Loopback Deadlock Avoidance
nodes.rationale: Loopback datagrams are enqueued and drained asynchronously in a clean context via net_poll/net_task to prevent TCP state machine re-entry mid-send, avoiding deadlocks in multi-packet exchanges.

nodes.label: Reaping Dead Task Slot Safety
nodes.rationale: TASK_REAPING prevents parent CPUs racing waitpid from double-freeing dead child task resources (kernel stack, page tables), avoiding a kernel UAF.

nodes.label: SMP Kernel Worker Stealing
nodes.rationale: Only CPU-bound kernel workers are stealable by APs because userspace tasks release the Big Kernel Lock but kernel paths are not yet SMP-safe.

nodes.label: Kernel Stack Lease
nodes.rationale: Uses volatile int stack_released to coordinate between CPU A running context switch away from dying task, and CPU B reaping it, to prevent freeing the stack while still in use.

nodes.label: Task Side Tables
nodes.rationale: Stores thread metadata (TID, TLS, Alarm, CPU times) in side tables to avoid growing struct task, which previously shifted kheap allocation order and triggered a latent page table bug.

nodes.label: tcp_conns connection table (32 slots)
nodes.rationale: 32 slots, not 16: the fork-per-connection SSH daemon occupies several slots per session (client conn + listener + accepted child) and SIGKILLed peers sit ~2s in TIME_WAIT, so the M32b SSH smoke's three back-to-back logins plus the white-box TCP tests would exhaust a 16-slot table (tcp_accept -> NULL).

nodes.label: Reno-shaped congestion control (M32)
nodes.rationale: Sliding-window flow control (snd_wnd refreshed on every segment) + slow start / congestion avoidance / fast retransmit on 3 dup-ACKs with RFC 5681 cwnd inflation. Send path honours min(cwnd, snd_wnd); framework is load-bearing for future TCP work even though current smoke traffic doesn't exercise window throttling.

nodes.label: ERESTARTSYS / SA_RESTART policy
nodes.rationale: On -ERESTARTSYS: if the first deliverable pending signal's handler has SA_RESTART (or default disposition), rewind rip by 2 (the syscall instruction) and re-arm rax to restart the syscall transparently; otherwise convert to -EINTR. This is how blocking I/O became signal-interruptible for nc/ping without breaking SA_RESTART users.

nodes.label: sys_utime i386 lo/hi time64 split
nodes.rationale: On i386 each 64-bit timestamp arrives split as lo/hi 32-bit args so post-2038 times survive the int $0x80 register ABI; x86_64 passes them whole.

nodes.label: M41 16 GiB firmware-map memory smoke
nodes.rationale: On-demand check that the x86_64 kernel sees >=15000 MiB usable from a 16G QEMU machine by grepping the 'pmm: firmware RAM' serial line — proves DIRECT_MAP_MAX large-RAM support.

nodes.label: POSIX shell/coreutils in-guest smoke (M11/M22-POLISH)
nodes.rationale: Runs INSIDE the guest under /bin/sh; each test emits a deterministic 'M11-SHELL: ok ...' marker that the host-side smoke.sh greps from the serial log. Ordered simple-to-complex so failures isolate easily.

nodes.label: M39 serial getty/login end-to-end test
nodes.rationale: Boots NORMAL mode (no b1nix.test, so the inittab supervisor runs), drives QEMU serial stdio with python3 as a real terminal: login as root, verify interactive bash via a guest-computed SERIAL-E2E-42 probe, exit, and confirm init respawns getty. Separate from smoke.sh because the supervisor never starts in test mode.

nodes.norm_label: smoke.sh main suite (build iso, boot, grep markers)

nodes.label: M32c external SSH hostfwd smoke
nodes.rationale: Separate from smoke.sh so CI never exposes a forwarded port by accident. The login marker EXTSSH-42-OK is computed ON the guest ($((6*7))) so it can never match the literal command echoed by expect — proving the remote shell actually ran. nc banner probe holds the connection open so a half-close doesn't abort the server's ident exchange.

nodes.label: b1nix-autotools-cc (autotools-aware CC wrapper)
nodes.rationale: Mimics a real compiler for configure scripts: -c/-E modes, version probes with no inputs forwarded straight to clang (linking crt0 there would fail 'undefined main' and confuse configure). Links crt0 + objects against libb1nix.a with the userspace linker script; B1NIX_LD_EXTRA env opt-in carries port-specific flags like bash's --allow-multiple-definition.

nodes.label: b1nix-buildcc (build-side flag-stripping wrapper)
nodes.rationale: GCC's native build leaks TARGET CXXFLAGS (--sysroot, -idirafter, -Wl,-Ttext-segment) into build-side gen* helpers that must compile with host flags; this wrapper strips those target-only flags using `set --` to preserve quoted -D defines, then execs the real host compiler.

nodes.label: build-bash.sh (GNU bash 5.2 port build)
nodes.rationale: Preseeded config.cache answers run-time probes a cross-compile cannot execute (job control, FIFOs, /dev/fd, sigsetjmp, bundled termcap). parse.y AND the shipped y.tab.c get the HANDLE_MULTIBYTE guard (macOS bison is too old to regenerate y.tab.c). -fcommon for K&R termcap tentative definitions; -D_POSIX_VERSION scoped to this build only (globally it flips OpenSSL to mlock b1nix lacks); --allow-multiple-definition keeps bash's own getenv/setenv set over libb1nix's. configure runs once because regenerating config.h is non-deterministic.

nodes.label: build-busybox.sh (upstream BusyBox 1.38 port build)
nodes.rationale: Widens '#ifdef __linux__' guards to __b1nix__ for sysinfo applets; stubs alloc_affinity (no CPU-affinity syscall); rewrites tree.c without scandir/alphasort while keeping the //config: metadata the kbuild scanner needs; patches pw_encrypt to defer '$b1$' salts to libc crypt() (builtin crypt died 'bad salt' and broke M39 serial login); force-cleans objects when libb1nix.a is newer than the binary because BusyBox make does not track sysroot headers; space-free sysroot symlink works around paths with spaces.

nodes.label: build-curl.sh (curl + mbedTLS port build)
nodes.rationale: Exports B1NIX_ARCH matching the triplet so every sub-make/libtool wrapper invocation compiles the right arch (a leaked CC=clang otherwise falls back to x86_64 and fails 'skipping incompatible' against i686 mbedTLS). Explicit --build distinct from --host so autoconf never RUNS a freshly compiled b1nix conftest (hangs forever on hosts with 32-bit binfmt).

nodes.label: build-dropbear.sh (Dropbear SSH port build)
nodes.rationale: Two phases (crypto-only archives vs full dropbearmulti). localoptions.h disables zlib/PAM/utmp/syslog so the build is self-contained. Configure runs ONCE: re-running showed non-deterministic HAVE_GETPASS detection leaving stale objects referencing rpl_getpass; locking the first good config.h makes incremental rebuilds reproducible.

nodes.label: build-libidn2.sh (static libidn2 port build)
nodes.rationale: Recreates the build dir from scratch every run (the autotools tree corrupts after interrupted cross builds) and builds -j1 because the tree is sensitive to jobserver propagation; depends on a prebuilt static libunistring.
